subject.title: Feature Request: Gateway lifecycle hooks (onSubagentComplete, onToolCallThreshold, onTurnComplete)

question: Should OpenClaw expose these lifecycle boundaries as workspace/internal hooks, typed plugin hooks, or a split design, and which payload fields are safe to publish?
rationale: The requested events would let local hook code react to subagent output, turn completion, and tool-call counts, so the permanent API and security boundary need maintainer intent before implementation.

options.title: Design contract first
options.body: Define event names, safe payloads, permissions, config semantics, docs, and tests before queuing implementation.

options.title: Keep lifecycle control plugin-only
options.body: Leave workspace hooks coarse and direct runtime lifecycle automation to typed plugin hooks.

options.title: Limit to subagent observation
options.body: Add only a minimal subagent completion observation event now and defer turn/threshold semantics to a later design.

recommendation.title: Design contract first
recommendation.body: Define event names, safe payloads, permissions, config semantics, docs, and tests before queuing implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest recent history around hook lifecycle docs and related lifecycle-hook PR direction.
